verdict.rationale: The guidance and forms pages on www.sos.state.tx.us were read verbatim, and the forms directory is described as published and downloadable without an account. That points to a keyless, unwalled public reading surface. However, no probe records HTTP status, user-agent handling, or the absence of a JS shell or CAPTCHA on that host. The sibling filing host's robots.txt also bans AI agents by name (GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot), so agent access across the service is not uniformly open. Missing for 10: a direct probe of www.sos.state.tx.us confirming HTTP 200 for an identified agent user agent, a robots.txt check of the guidance host, explicit confirmation of no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA, and agent access to the filing host, which disallows AI agents by name.

support.subject: As an AI-native founder, the service's published guidance pages are reachable by a keyless agent with a standard identified user agent — no bot wall, JS-only shell, or CAPTCHA in front of the public reading surface
